name: Mepolizumab
tagline: First anti-IL-5 antibody, lowering eosinophils in severe asthma and EGPA
summary: Mepolizumab is a humanised monoclonal antibody that neutralises interleukin-5, the main cytokine for eosinophil growth and survival. It is used for severe eosinophilic asthma, eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis, hypereosinophilic syndrome, nasal polyps and, since 2025 in the US, eosinophilic COPD.
mechanism: IL-5 drives eosinophil differentiation in bone marrow, their release into blood and their survival in tissues.
Mepolizumab binds IL-5 and prevents it from binding the IL-5 receptor α chain on eosinophils, lowering blood and sputum eosinophil counts and reducing eosinophil-driven exacerbations.
uses: Severe eosinophilic asthma (adults and children ≥6 years)

history.title: Early asthma study
history.detail: A study finds mepolizumab lowers eosinophils without changing the allergen response, dampening early enthusiasm.

history.title: DREAM
history.detail: DREAM shows fewer exacerbations in patients selected for eosinophilic asthma.

history.title: FDA and EU approval
history.detail: Approved in November (US) and December (EU) for severe eosinophilic asthma.

history.title: EGPA
history.detail: First drug approved for eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis.

history.title: Hypereosinophilic syndrome
history.detail: First new FDA approval for HES in 14 years.

history.title: Nasal polyps
history.detail: Approved for chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps.

history.title: COPD
history.detail: FDA approves mepolizumab for COPD with an eosinophilic phenotype (MATINEE).

pk.metabolism: Proteolytic catabolism to peptides and amino acids (no CYP metabolism)
pk.excretion: Not renally excreted as intact antibody; cleared by catabolism and target-mediated uptake

facts: Mepolizumab's development illustrates the value of selecting patients by biomarker: early trials in unselected asthma were disappointing.
It was the first drug approved for EGPA.
